**Claims check**

| Claim | Status |
|---|---|
| "Plastic-Free Tea Bags" (headline) | Allowlisted: "Our tea bags are plastic-free and home compostable" (supplier certificate, EN 13432) |
| "Our tea bags are plastic-free and home compostable" | Allowlisted, exact wording |
| "Recommended by nutritionists" | Unsupported. It's a social-proof/endorsement claim with no source in the allowlist, and it implies a health-professional endorsement. Health-adjacent territory is also never permitted by the brand policy, and platforms scrutinise it. |

**Other checks**
- Slop/banned words: none hit.
- Landing-page rule: any ad claim must also appear on the landing page. "Recommended by nutritionists" would need to be there too, and there's no proof for it.
- Character limits: none were given, so I haven't counted against a limit. Note that the headline as written is short, but real RSA headlines are capped at 30 characters. "Plastic-Free Tea Bags" is 21, so it's fine.
- Disclosure: this is our own paid ad, which the platform marks, so no extra label is needed.

**Verdict:** Do not publish as is. Remove "Recommended by nutritionists". If a replacement is wanted, use an allowlisted claim.

**Compliant version**
Headline: Plastic-Free Tea Bags
Description: Our tea bags are plastic-free and home compostable. Certified organic by the Soil Association.

(Alternative second sentence: "Free UK delivery on orders over £25.")
